note: Canonical enumeration of Duo-hostile code patterns. This file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. scripts/audit-duo.sh consumes it; SKILL.md and references/06 point at it instead of re-listing regexes. Add a pattern here and every consumer picks it up.

categories.title: Global screen geometry
categories.why: UIScreen.main is ambiguous on a two-display device and will be deprecated. Global geometry cannot describe a resizable, asymmetric, possibly-split container.
categories.fix: window?.windowScene?.screen for the screen; traitCollection.displayScale for scale; GeometryReader / scene bounds for size.

categories.title: Device-identity layout branch
categories.why: Layout must react to available space, not to which device or which display it is running on. Identity branches produce two divergent UIs that drift.
categories.fix: Size classes, container geometry, ViewThatFits/AnyLayout, or a real minimum-content-width threshold.

categories.title: Orientation used as a layout switch
categories.why: The inner display does not honor supported interface orientations, and is regular in BOTH dimensions. Orientation is not a proxy for available space. Declaring an orientation policy for a game is different and is intentionally not matched here.
categories.fix: horizontalSizeClass / verticalSizeClass, or measured container width, for layout decisions.

categories.title: Hardcoded screen-derived dimensions
categories.why: Apple does not publish iPhone Duo logical point sizes or native scale. Any copied device constant is a guess that breaks on resize and in Split View.
categories.fix: Container-relative sizing; thresholds only where they express a real minimum usable content width.

categories.title: Fixed grid column count
categories.why: A fixed column count is an ordinary adaptability risk before it is a Duo-specific fold concern. The grid should first respond to available width; when a fold is relevant, then verify that the resulting expansive count divides cleanly around it.
categories.fix: Prefer GridItem(.adaptive(minimum:)) or a content-derived adaptive layout. Apply fold/even-column tuning only after the universal grid is responsive.

categories.title: Custom bar instead of a system bar
categories.why: Only container-provided bars participate in the vertical bar region. Content in a hand-rolled UIToolbar/UINavigationBar/UITabBar is not considered, and cannot overflow or reorient automatically.
categories.fix: NavigationStack/NavigationSplitView + .toolbar, or UINavigationController/UITabBarController, when the interaction fits system bar semantics.

categories.title: Manual spacing inside a bar
categories.why: Flexible spacers have zero size on the vertical axis. Manual spacing collapses or misaligns when the bar rotates.
categories.fix: ToolbarItemGroup / UIBarButtonItemGroup, which space themselves and adapt.

categories.title: Hinge input driving ordinary layout
categories.why: Apple is explicit: hinge data is for interactions and effects, not ordinary layout. Layout belongs to available-space, arrangement, and reserved-region APIs.
categories.fix: Use available space, reservedRegions(kind:), or ArrangementView for layout; keep onHingeChange for physical interaction only.

categories.title: Legacy builtInDuoCamera false friend
categories.why: AVCaptureDevice.DeviceType.builtInDuoCamera is a deprecated iOS 10 alias for the rear dual camera and has no relationship to iPhone Duo. Its name makes it especially likely to be adopted incorrectly by code-generation agents.
categories.fix: For ordinary user-facing capture, discover the virtual front camera. For explicit Duo physical-camera control, use the manifested iOS 27.1 camera types and AVCaptureDeviceDirectionCoordinator after SDK verification.

categories.title: Duo API adoption surface
categories.why: Not a defect — an inventory of which Duo APIs the codebase already touches, so the audit can report adoption depth.

categories.title: Parallel compact/expanded state
categories.why: Two sources of truth for one feature means folding or resizing can silently lose navigation path, selection, drafts or playback.
categories.fix: One state owner; adaptive presentation reads from it.
